analysis: Examined two base-side excerpts (lines 50237-52131) of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json. The file is a golden-vector test fixture holding request bodies, provider bodies, template inputs, prompt plans (prompt_contract_id, block-boundary chain hashes) and token IDs for the Qwen model. The patch excerpt shows the change adds an "additional_context": {"enable_thinking": false} field to some vectors and changes token counts and chain hashes, which are regenerated expected values. The visible base excerpts only show unchanged-context vectors, and the patch excerpt is truncated, so the head side was not visible. I saw no executable code, secrets, credentials, endpoint or authorization changes, and no change to the encryption, attestation or App Attest boundaries (TB-002, TB-011). The fixture content is synthetic (fixture-scope, 2028 date). Security-relevant considerations for downstream passes: (1) the prompt-contract/prefix-cache identity (T-041) depends on prompt_contract_id and chain hashes. The new additional_context field must be included in the contract and cache-key derivation so that thinking-mode variants do not share cache blocks across different rendered prompts, and this belongs to the provider/coordinator code that was not supplied. (2) The fixture changes should match the code changes in whichever Swift/Go sources define the template rendering. A mismatch would be a correctness problem, not a security finding. No concrete regression is identifiable from this fixture-only evidence. Coverage limit: the head text and the non-fixture sources were not supplied.
